mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses the discount rate for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% over a 3-month period signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a slowdown in corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate revenue growth slows.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of rising industrial production (INDPRO), the supply chain is tightening, which typically leads to higher inflation and monetary policy tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is rising, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over the past 6 months indicates strong consumer spending, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS has increased over the prior 6 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic growth slows.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and corporate profits are pressured.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 over the past 3 months signals a weakening manufacturing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as economic growth slows.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 105.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
